key_insight: Positioning a passive phononic subsurface beneath a separated flat-plate flow can shift sustained vortex shedding from amplification to strong attenuation.
engineering_relevance: A favorable configuration reduced lift oscillation amplitude by over 30% and drag oscillation amplitude by over 50%, with less than 0.5% change in mean lift and drag.
method: Simulated strongly coupled, nonlinear fluid–structure interaction using a high-fidelity immersed boundary method.
Modeled the phononic subsurface as a grounded diatomic chain driving a compliant plate section.
Varied chordwise position and resonant displacement-amplitude growth rate; analyzed frequencies, phase relationships, and flow fields.
evidence_signal: Simulations identified four position-dependent limit-cycle regimes, while displacement-amplitude growth primarily affected transient responsiveness in a position-dependent manner.
watch_item: Placement requires careful tuning: some positions amplify oscillations, and the abstract provides simulation rather than experimental validation.
paper_title: Interaction of Sustained Vortex Shedding with a Phononic Subsurface: Effect of Positioning and Resonant Characteristics
